findings.title: Corrupted Files, Non-Source Binaries, and Malformed Path Names Breaking Test Runners
findings.where: Testing/Mq5/--+---------------------------.docx:1, Testing/Mq5/brains.mq5 kgaugelo:1, Testing/Mq5/Simple_Classic_Trailing.mq5:1, Testing/Mq5/FIB 2.mq5:1, Testing/Mq5/VSA Indicator´s Simple Weis Wave .mq5:1
findings.failure: Build scripts and transpiler runner globs (`*.mq5`) fail to match `brains.mq5 kgaugelo`, crash on invalid UTF-8 / corrupted space files (`Simple_Classic_Trailing.mq5`), fail on empty 0-line files (`FIB 2.mq5`), fail to parse Word document archives (`--+---------------------------.docx`), and fail on non-standard Unicode accent characters across cross-platform CI systems.
findings.fix: Normalize filenames, remove binary Word documents and empty/corrupted files, and ensure all files are valid UTF-8/UTF-16 text with `.mq5` or `.mqh` extensions.

findings.title: Remote Control Channel and Unauthenticated Command Execution via Telegram `WebRequest` Polling
findings.failure: When executed in an environment with network access enabled, `PollTelegramCommands()` polls the external Telegram HTTP API on every timer cycle. It parses JSON payloads and executes remote commands (`/pause`, `/resume`, `/report`), while `SendTelegram()` exfiltrates live account balance, equity, and open positions to third-party endpoints.
findings.fix: Remove background Telegram HTTP polling from test EAs and enforce strict network mocking in backtesting and transpiler test harnesses.

findings.title: Hardcoded Expiration Timebomb Disabling Backtests and Live Execution Past April 2026
findings.failure: When `7.mq5`, `8.mq5`, or `titan v1.3.mq5` is backtested or executed with simulation/system timestamps beyond 2026-04-15 23:59, `OnInit()` immediately aborts with `INIT_FAILED` and `OnTick()` returns without processing orders, causing all test runs and historical backtests past that date to silently fail.
findings.fix: Delete the hardcoded `Internal_Expiry` checks from test strategies.

findings.title: Hardcoded kill-switch expiration dates in `7.mq5` and `8.mq5` halt execution after April 15, 2026
findings.failure: Both `7.mq5` (`TITAN_NO_LOSS_ULTIMATE.mq5`) and `8.mq5` (`TITAN_ULTIMATE_STEALTH_AI.mq5`) contain hardcoded anti-piracy kill-switches set to `D'2026.04.15 23:59'`. Any backtest run or live forward test spanning past April 15, 2026 fails initialization with `INIT_FAILED` or silently aborts `OnTick` execution.
findings.fix: Remove the `Internal_Expiry` constant and associated validation guards from `OnInit()` and `OnTick()`.

findings.title: Broken position counting in `9od10leporadi.mq5` repeatedly evaluates the first symbol position and bypasses max trade limits
findings.failure: In MT5 hedging accounts, `PositionSelect(symbol)` only selects the first open position matching the symbol. In a loop of `PositionsTotal()` iterations, `PositionSelect(symbol)` selects the identical position ticket on every iteration. If an initial BUY position exists, `CountOpenPositions(1)` returns `PositionsTotal()`, while `CountOpenPositions(-1)` returns 0 regardless of how many SELL positions are open. The `currentOpenTrades >= MaxTrades` guard never triggers for SELL trades, leading to unbounded order spamming on every tick until margin exhaustion.
findings.fix: Replace `PositionSelect(symbol)` with index selection using `ulong ticket = PositionGetTicket((int)i); if (PositionSelectByTicket(ticket))`.

findings.title: Missing logical OR operators in `Ashu_Gold_EA_FINAL_V3.mq5` causes syntax error and compilation failure
findings.failure: The `if` condition omits the logical OR operators (`||`), separating the operand comparisons with whitespace. The MQL5 compiler and transpiler parser reject the token sequence with a syntax error (`'handleEMA200' - semicolon expected`), completely blocking compilation of the EA.
findings.fix: Restore the missing operators: `if(handleEMA50 == INVALID_HANDLE || handleEMA200 == INVALID_HANDLE || handleATR == INVALID_HANDLE)`.

findings.title: Win32 DLL automation and MT5 GUI window messaging in `AutoTrading Scheduler.mqh`
findings.failure: `AutoTrading Scheduler.mqh` imports `user32.dll` to find the MT5 root window and send `WM_COMMAND` 33020 (the native AutoTrading toolbar toggle button). In a .NET backtest engine or Linux container, `user32.dll` P/Invoke calls throw `DllNotFoundException` or `EntryPointNotFoundException`, and Windows message routing does not exist.
findings.fix: Abstract automated trading scheduling behind an internal engine state flag rather than invoking native Win32 window message queues.

findings.title: Missing include guards permit duplicate symbol definitions
findings.failure: `AutoTrading Scheduler.mqh`, `Defines.mqh`, `GammaAccelerationEngine.mqh`, and `GammaAccelerationEngineMulti.mqh` contain neither `#ifndef` macro guards nor `#property once` / `#pragma once`. If any of these headers are included by more than one file in a compilation unit, class definitions (`CScheduler`), helper functions, and global constants are defined multiple times, causing compiler redeclaration errors.
findings.fix: Add standard `#ifndef` include guard macros or `#property once` at the beginning of all four header files.

findings.title: Native Win32 DLL import breaks cross-platform execution
findings.failure: `AutoTrading Scheduler.mqh` imports native `user32.dll` to find the MT5 parent window handle and simulate mouse click messages on the AutoTrading button. When transpiled to C# or executed in Linux containerized backtesting engines, native Windows P/Invoke calls fail with `DllNotFoundException` or `EntryPointNotFoundException`.
findings.fix: Provide managed transpiler abstraction for trading enablement flags instead of invoking native desktop Win32 APIs.

findings.title: Empty button name in `BOT TP AND SL.mq5` causes `ObjectCreate` failure and disabled UI controls
findings.failure: `button_name` is initialized to empty string `""`. In MQL5, `ObjectCreate(0, "", ...)` fails with error 4001/5038 because graphical objects must possess a non-empty name. The GUI button is never created on the chart, and chart click events in `OnChartEvent` comparing `sparam == button_name` fail to match.
findings.fix: Initialize `string button_name = "btn_ToggleEA";`.

findings.title: Inverted EMA crossover logic and unselected position trailing in `BTC_EMA_Crossover_TSL_EA_Hedging.mq5`
findings.failure: Dynamic arrays populated via `CopyBuffer` without `ArraySetAsSeries(arr, true)` store elements chronologically (`[0]` is bar 1 / older bar, `[1]` is bar 0 / newest bar). The condition `fastEMA[1] < slowEMA[1] && fastEMA[0] > slowEMA[0]` evaluates `current_fast < current_slow && prev_fast > prev_slow` (a bearish death cross), yet invokes `OpenOrder(ORDER_TYPE_BUY)`. Conversely, a golden cross triggers `OpenOrder(ORDER_TYPE_SELL)`. Furthermore, lines 86-95 invoke `PositionGetInteger(POSITION_TYPE)` and `PositionGetDouble(POSITION_SL)` in `ManageTrailingStop()` after removing `PositionSelect`, returning 0 for all fields and sending malformed SL modification requests on every tick while failing to trail open positions.
findings.fix: Add `ArraySetAsSeries(fastEMA, true); ArraySetAsSeries(slowEMA, true);` in `OnTick()` and iterate through open positions with `PositionGetTicket(i)` in `ManageTrailingStop()`.

findings.title: Undeclared identifier `MAGIC_NUMBER` and legacy MQL4 trading functions in `Breakout_EA (1).mq5`
findings.failure: `MAGIC_NUMBER` is referenced on lines 57 and 64 but is never declared or defined anywhere in the file. Compiling or transpiling this file fails immediately with `'MAGIC_NUMBER' - undeclared identifier`. Furthermore, the file uses MQL4 `OrderSend`, `OrdersTotal`, `OrderSelect`, and `OrderModify` APIs inside an `.mq5` container while indexing `rates[1]` without setting timeseries orientation (evaluating 20 bars in the past).
findings.fix: Declare `input ulong MAGIC_NUMBER = 123456;` and migrate the order execution logic to `CTrade::Buy` and `CTrade::Sell`.

findings.title: Reverse buffer indexing in `CRUDE_OIL_EMA_Crossover_TSL_EA.mq5` inverts buy and sell signals
findings.failure: When `CopyBuffer` copies into dynamic arrays without `ArraySetAsSeries(arr, true)`, MQL5 stores data in standard chronological order (`[0]` is bar 1 / older bar, `[1]` is bar 0 / newest bar). The check `fastEMA[1] < slowEMA[1] && fastEMA[0] > slowEMA[0]` evaluates `current_fast < current_slow && prev_fast > prev_slow` (a bearish crossover / death cross), yet executes `OpenOrder(ORDER_TYPE_BUY)`. Conversely, a golden cross triggers `OpenOrder(ORDER_TYPE_SELL)`. The EA executes trades 100% in reverse of its designed strategy.
findings.fix: Call `ArraySetAsSeries(fastEMA, true); ArraySetAsSeries(slowEMA, true);` before `CopyBuffer`, or invert the index checks to `fastEMA[0] > slowEMA[0] && fastEMA[1] < slowEMA[1]` for bullish entries.

findings.title: Redundant identical files and unextracted archive committed to test corpus
findings.where: Testing/Mq5/CrudeOilScalpEA (2).mq5:1, Testing/Mq5/CrudeOilScalpEA (3).mq5:1, Testing/Mq5/Elise-EA (2).mq5:1, Testing/Mq5/Crude oil scalper.zip:1
findings.failure: Duplicate copies bloat test execution runs with redundant evaluations, while `Crude oil scalper.zip` contains unextracted `.mq5` and `.ex5` files that are ignored by test runners.
findings.fix: Remove duplicate files and extract archive contents into distinct test fixtures.

findings.title: Invalid `OnDeinit` signature and deprecated MQL4 plotting functions in `DAY TRADING FOREX.txt` prevent MQL5 compilation
findings.failure: In MQL5, `OnDeinit` must return `void`. Returning `int` with `return(INIT_SUCCEEDED)` fails compilation with `'OnDeinit' - function must return 'void'`. Furthermore, lines 72-78 call legacy MQL4 APIs (`SetIndexStyle`, `SetIndexArrow`, `IndicatorDigits`) which do not exist in the MQL5 runtime.
findings.fix: Change return type to `void OnDeinit(const int reason)` (removing the return value) and migrate indicator styling to `PlotIndexSetInteger` / `IndicatorSetInteger`.

findings.title: Global variable definition in header file `Defines.mqh` causes duplicate symbol linker collision
findings.failure: `Defines.mqh` instantiates the global variable `sets` directly in header scope. If `Defines.mqh` is included in multiple compilation units, the MQL5 compiler and transpiler linker fail with duplicate identifier errors (`'sets' already defined`).
findings.fix: Remove variable instantiation from the struct definition and declare `extern Settings sets;` in headers or instantiate locally inside `.mq5` files.

findings.title: UTF-16LE encoding without BOM in `EA Correlations.mq5` breaks UTF-8 transpiler tokenizers
findings.failure: `EA Correlations.mq5` (481,708 bytes) is stored in 16-bit little-endian Unicode without a 0xFF 0xFE BOM header. Standard UTF-8 decoders interpret every alternate byte as `0x00` (NUL), causing lexical analyzers to encounter unexpected null characters and abort parsing.
findings.fix: Enhance file ingestion to detect alternating null bytes in header preambles and decode using UTF-16LE fallback when no BOM is present.

findings.title: Synchronous WebRequest in `EA-MT5-OPENAI.mq5` blocks tick processing for up to 10 seconds and crashes in strategy tester
findings.failure: Executing a blocking HTTP POST with a 10-second timeout inside the main `OnTick` / `OnTimer` thread freezes order execution, stops, and tick tracking during high market volatility. Additionally, MT5 prohibits `WebRequest` during backtests (returning error 4060 / ERR_FUNCTION_NOT_ALLOWED), forcing the EA into fallback mode on every test run.
findings.fix: Decouple LLM calls into asynchronous background workers and inject mock response fixtures for deterministic backtesting.

findings.title: Hardcoded 2-decimal lot normalization in `EA_ULTRA_AGGRESSIVE.mq5` causes invalid volume errors on non-forex assets
findings.failure: Hardcoding `NormalizeDouble(lot, 2)` forces trade volume to 2 decimal places. On crypto pairs with 3-decimal precision (e.g., 0.001 min lot) or indices with 0-decimal integer lots (e.g., US30 lot step 1.0), this normalization produces invalid lot sizes that trigger `TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_VOLUME`.
findings.fix: Compute lot precision dynamically from `sym.LotsStep()` instead of hardcoding 2 decimals.

findings.title: Truncated 3-byte stub file `FIB 2.mq5` causes unexpected EOF parser error
findings.failure: `FIB 2.mq5` is a 3-byte file consisting exclusively of a UTF-8 Byte Order Mark with 0 lines of code. Compilers and transpilers attempting to parse this compilation unit encounter an unexpected end of file.
findings.fix: Filter out and quarantine files with byte size <= 3 during corpus ingestion.

findings.title: Synchronous AI/Cloud `WebRequest` calls freeze tick execution and fail in strategy tester
findings.failure: In `GoldScalpingEA-1.mq5` (and similarly in `MB_Sniper EA v1.mq5:802`, `Hon-Matrix.mq5:430`, `GoldReaper_MT5_ECN_Patched (1).mq5:9933`, and `Lizard_1.85.mq5:10304`), synchronous `WebRequest` calls with up to 30,000ms timeouts are invoked from the main execution thread. findings.title: Generic include guard macro collision suppresses independent header loading
findings.failure: `Key_levels_Ulli.mqh`, `Key_levels_Ulli (2).mqh`, and `Key_levels_Ulli (3).mqh` all use the generic guard `#ifndef ALREADY_INCLUDED`. If any other library or script defines `ALREADY_INCLUDED`, or if a strategy attempts to include both an indicator and key levels header, the preprocessor silently skips the entire contents of `Key_levels_Ulli.mqh`. Furthermore, the file defines naked global variables (`extern calc_methods calculation_method ...`) in the header scope, causing duplicate symbol linker collisions upon multiple inclusions.
findings.fix: Replace `ALREADY_INCLUDED` with unique include guard symbols (e.g. `KEY_LEVELS_ULLI_MQH`) and encapsulate global variables inside static class members or local namespaces.

findings.title: Compiled binary file committed with `.mq5` source extension in `Lopez Strategy EA.mq5` breaks transpilers
findings.failure: `Lopez Strategy EA.mq5` (289,472 bytes) is not an MQL5 text source file but a compiled `.ex5` binary executable from fxDreema starting with the `EX-` magic header. Source transpilers and lexers attempting to parse this file crash on non-text binary bytes.
findings.fix: Rename the file to `Lopez Strategy EA.ex5` and add magic byte validation to reject binary files in source ingestion pipelines.

findings.title: UTF-16LE encoding without BOM in `MM3.0 FLIP CODEPRO.mq5` breaks UTF-8 stream readers
findings.where: Testing/Mq5/MM3.0 FLIP CODEPRO.mq5:1, Testing/Mq5/MM3.0 FLIP CODEPRO (2).mq5:1
findings.failure: `MM3.0 FLIP CODEPRO.mq5` (523,482 bytes, 9,384 lines) and `MM3.0 FLIP CODEPRO (2).mq5` (528,534 bytes, 9,446 lines) are encoded in 16-bit little-endian Unicode without a 0xFF 0xFE BOM header. Standard UTF-8 stream readers encounter alternating null bytes (`0x00`), causing lexical analyzers to terminate parsing.
findings.fix: Implement null-byte preamble inspection to detect BOM-less UTF-16LE files during ingestion.

findings.title: Native `user32.dll` `#import` for MetaTrader GUI Button and Process Hijacking
findings.failure: The EA imports unmanaged Win32 GUI APIs (`user32.dll`) to search the desktop window tree via `GetAncestor` and post Windows window messages (`WM_COMMAND` with ID `32851` / `33020`) to toggle the terminal's global AutoTrading button. When executed in the C# transpiler, backtester engine, or headless/Linux container, these unmanaged DLL imports trigger runtime memory faults, unhandled P/Invoke exceptions, or unauthorized desktop interaction.
findings.fix: Remove `#import "user32.dll"` and GUI manipulation logic; use standard MQL5 runtime API state checks or mock abstractions.

findings.title: Out-of-sandbox Win32 DLL import via #import (News Stopper MT5.mq5)

In a containerized Linux execution environment or secure sandbox, native Win32 DLL imports fail to link and are blocked with `MQL5_LOWER_UNSUPPORTED_IMPORT_BODY`, terminating the compilation.
findings.fix: Quarantine or filter DLL imports in the ingestion pre-pass and stub user32 messaging routines for headless execution.

findings.title: Unhandled C++ template class declarations and BOM-less UTF-16 in visual EA (Prop-Firm Expert.mq5)
findings.failure: `Prop-Firm Expert.mq5` (523,834 bytes, 9,602 lines) is encoded in UTF-16LE without a Byte Order Mark and contains multi-type C++ template classes. When passed to `Mql5Lowering.Lower()`, the lowering engine hits `UnsupportedTemplate` (`MQL5_LOWER_UNSUPPORTED_TEMPLATE`) and poisons the module (`Module: null`), preventing transpilation of visual builder EAs.
findings.fix: Add a template monomorphization/specialization pass in the front end or flag fxDreema template visual components as unsupported prior to lowering.

findings.title: Shared Common File System Trial Lock Escape via `FILE_COMMON`
findings.failure: The strategy writes and checks trial timestamps in `%APPDATA%\MetaQuotes\Terminal\Common\Files\quantum_queen_x_mt5_42_14d_b.dat` using `FILE_COMMON`. When executed outside the tester environment for >14 days, the EA sets `g_trial_expired = true` and silently disables order execution, while mutating global files across terminal instances on the host.
findings.fix: Remove file-based trial locking routines from test strategies.

findings.title: Blocking GUI MessageBox dialogs and common filesystem trial probing (Quantum Queen X 4.3.mq5)
findings.failure: During `OnInit()`, the strategy checks a trial expiration file in the shared common directory (`FileOpen(QQ_TRIAL_FILE, FILE_READ|FILE_TXT|FILE_COMMON)` at line 256). If the trial is expired, it calls `MessageBox()` at line 326. In headless backtests or automated cloud runners, `MessageBox()` blocks the thread awaiting interactive UI confirmation that never arrives, hanging the runner worker indefinitely.
findings.fix: Stub `MessageBox` to log a warning and return `IDOK`/`IDCANCEL` immediately without blocking in non-interactive backtesting runtimes.

findings.title: MQL4 legacy indicator file present in MQL5 test corpus (SHK Professional Heikin Ashi 1.00.mq4)
findings.failure: `SHK Professional Heikin Ashi 1.00.mq4` is an MQL4 indicator file placed inside the MQL5 corpus directory. It contains legacy MQL4 indicator buffer declarations (`#property indicator_buffers 10`, `SetIndexBuffer()`, `IndicatorDigits()`, `WindowRedraw()`) which fail MQL5 parsing and lexing passes.

findings.title: Naked pointer allocation and deallocation without null checks (SetFixedSLandTP.mq5)
findings.failure: `Trade` is dynamically allocated via `new CTrade` on every call to `SetFixedSLandTP()` (line 80) and destroyed via `delete Trade;` (line 424) without checking allocation success (`CheckPointer(Trade)`). If an early return occurs (e.g. at line 91, 102, or 120), `delete Trade;` is bypassed, creating repeated memory leaks on every tick in unmanaged MQL5 execution.
findings.fix: Declare `CTrade Trade;` as an automatic/stack variable or class member rather than allocating and deleting dynamic pointers inside a high-frequency tick routine.

findings.title: All-NUL corrupted file in test corpus (Simple_Classic_Trailing.mq5)
findings.failure: `Simple_Classic_Trailing.mq5` consists of 7,156 bytes of pure `0x00` (NUL) characters with 0 valid lines of code. When ingested by `Mql5SourceDecoder.Decode()`, it is flagged as `Mql5SourceContentKind.AllNul` (`MQL5_FRONTEND_ALL_NUL_SOURCE`) and compilation is rejected. Meanwhile, the valid source code exists alongside it under the name `Simple Classic Trailing Stop Mq5.txt`.
findings.fix: Replace `Simple_Classic_Trailing.mq5` with the contents of `Simple Classic Trailing Stop Mq5.txt` and delete the stray `.txt` file.

findings.title: Division by zero in THEHFT lot sizing during zero-stoploss execution
findings.failure: When `LotType > 0` and `CalculatedStopLoss` is 0 (or `ticksize` is 0 before symbol quotes initialize), `slPoints` is 0, causing `moneyPerLotstep` to evaluate to `0.0`. The subsequent division `risk / moneyPerLotstep` divides by zero, resulting in `+Infinity` / `NaN`. `MathFloor` and subsequent math bounds fail, producing invalid trade volumes and throwing runtime floating point exceptions during execution.
findings.fix: Add a non-zero guard checking `if (slPoints <= 0 || ticksize <= 0 || tickvalue <= 0 || lotstep <= 0) return fixedLots;` before computing `moneyPerLotstep`.

findings.title: Redundant duplicate strategy and include files inflate corpus maintenance
findings.failure: The corpus contains near-identical duplicate files with minor whitespace or comment changes: `Thanos EA Source Code.mq5`, `Thanos V1.0.mq5`, `Thanos V1.0 (2).mq5`, and `Thanos V1.0 (3).mq5`; `UT Bot.mq5` and `UT Bot (2).mq5`; `Key_levels_Ulli.mqh`, `Key_levels_Ulli (2).mqh`, and `Key_levels_Ulli (3).mqh`; and `EATelemetry.mqh` vs `EATelemetry (2).mqh`. This inflates test matrix execution time without providing additional semantic coverage.
findings.fix: Deduplicate identical strategies and keep canonical, version-tagged single copies in the verification test suite.

findings.title: Compiled MT4 binary artifact in MQL5 source corpus
findings.failure: `The Gold Reaper 4.1 Enhanced.ex4` is a compiled MetaTrader 4 binary file placed inside the MQL5 source directory. Any source transpiler or lexical analyzer attempting to read the test corpus as text will encounter raw binary bytecode, triggering encoding crashes or syntax parse failures.

findings.title: Synchronous external WebRequest and modal UI dialog halt execution and corrupt time calculations
findings.failure: In offline, headless, or backtest environments, `WebRequest` to external endpoints is disallowed or unavailable. The code triggers a blocking modal `MessageBox` that freezes the engine thread, returns a fallback code `"999"` which sets GMT offset calculation to 999 hours, and permanently disables trading time window filters.
findings.fix: Replace external HTTP web time scraping with standard broker server time API calls (`TimeTradeServer()` / `TimeGMT()`) and remove modal `MessageBox` calls.

file: Testing/Mq5/The REAL-GAINS Algo MT5 M1 EA.mq5

findings.title: Unhandled zero tick size causes division by zero in lot size and pip value calculations
findings.where: Testing/Mq5/The REAL-GAINS Algo MT5 M1 EA.mq5:186
findings.failure: On custom symbol feeds, synthetic instruments, or during engine initialization before symbol market data is resolved, `sym.TickSize()` returns `0.0`. Evaluating `stopDistance / tickSize` produces `NaN`/`Infinity`, causing `lossPerLot` evaluation to fail and corrupting risk-based lot sizing across trades (identical bug present in `XAUUSD XARD FX EA SOURCE CODE.mq5:171`).
findings.fix: Check `if (tickSize <= 0.0) return minLot;` immediately after retrieving `tickSize` prior to division.

findings.title: Decompiled Commercial EAs with Hex-Rays / IDA Pro Disassembly Artifacts
findings.failure: Commercial third-party EAs decompiled via binary disassemblers (Hex-Rays, IDA Pro, ex4-to-mq4) were committed to the test suite with raw stack variable names (`qword_6B59578`, `dword_6B59714`) and explicit piracy attribution headers. findings.title: Missing include files prevent compilation of multiple strategies

findings.title: Cleartext Account Number and Broker Identifier Exfiltration in Trailing Stop Notifications
findings.failure: On every trailing stop trigger, the EA extracts the broker company name (`ACCOUNT_COMPANY`), account holder's full legal name (`ACCOUNT_NAME`), and account number (`ACCOUNT_LOGIN`), broadcasting them in unencrypted plaintext via SMTP email and mobile push notifications (`SendNotification`), leaking account credentials and PII.

findings.title: Embedded Personal Email Addresses and Social Media Leaks in File Headers
findings.where: Testing/Mq5/UT Bot.mq5:10, Testing/Mq5/cm_SL-NL-TP.mq5:2, Testing/Mq5/SureForexHedging 1.09 a.mq5:9, Testing/Mq5/SMCstarV02.mq5:7, Testing/Mq5/Linear Regression Line.mq5:5, Testing/Mq5/RSIOMA.mq5:5

findings.title: BOM-less UTF-16LE file encoding corrupts standard text parsers
findings.failure: `XAU-GU Scalper.mq5` (12,861 lines, 498,758 bytes) is encoded in Little-Endian UTF-16 but lacks a 2-byte BOM (`0xFF 0xFE`). Standard UTF-8/ASCII readers interpret the stream as containing alternating null bytes `\0`, resulting in truncated file reads or parser syntax errors.
findings.fix: Normalize all source files in the corpus to UTF-8 with or without standard BOM via an automated repository encoding migration script.

findings.title: Extreme template meta-programming and dynamic object allocation complexity
findings.failure: `XAU-GU Scalper.mq5` uses 14-parameter template classes, pointer-based dynamic array allocation (`new Block19()`, `delete _blocks_[i]`), and hundreds of templated type coercions. `TopBottomEA.mq5:2396`, `Volume Profile Source Code.mq5:357`, and `VP Range V6 Source Code.mq5:433` similarly use generic template functions. Transpiling MQL5 templates to C# generics requires extensive type inference and monomorphization support in the transpiler.
findings.fix: Define transpiler template specialization lowering rules that monomorphize templated methods into concrete type overloads.

file: Testing/Mq5/XAUUSD XARD FX EA SOURCE CODE.mq5

findings.title: Broken quote currency extraction for non-6-character symbols
findings.where: Testing/Mq5/XAUUSD XARD FX EA SOURCE CODE.mq5:178
findings.failure: Hardcoding `StringSubstr(symbol, 3, 3)` assumes exactly a 6-character currency pair (e.g. `EURUSD` -> `USD`). For equities, indices, and suffixed broker symbols (e.g. `TSLA.nas`, `US500`, `BTCUSD_i`, `EURUSD.m`), `StringSubstr(symbol, 3, 3)` extracts invalid 3-character strings like `A.n`, `500`, or `USD_`. The subsequent `SymbolInfoDouble(conversionPair, SYMBOL_BID)` lookups fail, causing pip values to fall back to an arbitrary hardcoded exchange rate of 1.3.
findings.fix: Query `SymbolInfoString(symbol, SYMBOL_CURRENCY_PROFIT)` or `SYMBOL_CURRENCY_MARGIN` rather than slicing symbol string names.

findings.title: Unbounded indicator handle allocation in `brains.mq5 kgaugelo` leaks handles on every tick
findings.failure: `brains.mq5 kgaugelo` invokes `iMA` and `iDeMarker` inside `OnTick()` without calling `IndicatorRelease()`. In MetaTrader 5 and deterministic backtesting engines, indicator handles are finite resources tracked in a global handle table. Creating two handles per tick exhausts the handle table within minutes, triggering runtime error 4001 (`ERR_INDICATOR_CANNOT_CREATE`) and stopping all indicator evaluations.
findings.fix: Move indicator handle initialization into `OnInit()` and store handles in global variables.

findings.title: Inverted TakeProfit recalculation in `cm_SL-NL-TP.mq5` overwrites TakeProfit with Stoploss distance
findings.failure: In `cm_SL-NL-TP.mq5`, when a Buy position's calculated TP is at or below the Ask price (line 58) or a Sell position's TP is at or above Bid (line 94), the code attempts to shift the TP beyond current market price. However, line 58 adds `Stoploss * _Point` instead of `Takeprofit * _Point` (and line 94 subtracts `Stoploss * _Point`). If `Stoploss` is 500 points and `Takeprofit` is 200 points, invalid TPs are enlarged by 250%, distorting risk-reward parameters.
findings.fix: Replace `+ Stoploss * _Point` on line 58 and `- Stoploss * _Point` on line 94 with `+ Takeprofit * _Point` and `- Takeprofit * _Point`.

findings.title: Missing `request.symbol` in `cm_SL-NL-TP.mq5` causes `TRADE_ACTION_SLTP` rejection on strict brokers
findings.failure: `cm_SL-NL-TP.mq5` zeroes `request` and sets `request.position`, `request.sl`, `request.tp`, and `request.action = TRADE_ACTION_SLTP`, but leaves `request.symbol` empty. On brokers requiring symbol specification on order modifications, `OrderSend` returns false with retcode 10013 (`TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_REQUEST`).
findings.fix: Assign `request.symbol = _Symbol;` before calling `OrderSend`.

findings.title: Deal history inspection in `free_money_expert_robot_bot_hide_sl_and_tp_fixed_for_backtest.mq5` inspects entry deals and breaks Martingale lot sizing
findings.failure: In MT5, position opening deals (`DEAL_ENTRY_IN`) also possess `DEAL_TYPE_BUY` or `DEAL_TYPE_SELL` with `DEAL_PROFIT == 0.0`. When a position is entered, its entry deal becomes the latest deal in history. Because line 85 checks `if (profit >= 0) currentLot = LotSize;`, the EA evaluates the newly opened entry deal as a winning exit, immediately resetting `currentLot` back to `LotSize` and destroying the Martingale multiplier progression after losses.
findings.fix: Add `&& HistoryDealGetInteger(ticket, DEAL_ENTRY) == DEAL_ENTRY_OUT` to the deal inspection filter so only closed trade deals are evaluated for profit calculation.

findings.title: Hardcoded expiration date kill-switch in `heaven and hell.mq5` permanently aborts initialization
findings.failure: `OnInit()` executes `if (!CheckExpiry()) return INIT_FAILED;` on line 610. Because `ExpiryDate` is hardcoded to "2025.11.30", running this EA in live trading in 2026 or running a backtest spanning dates past November 2025 causes `OnInit()` to immediately return `INIT_FAILED`, completely halting execution.
findings.fix: Remove the `CheckExpiry` call or set `ExpiryDate` to an unrestricted default value.

findings.title: MQL4 `iMA` invocation signature in `mt DanielScalper.mq5` causes compilation failure and corrupted trend evaluation
findings.failure: In MQL5, `iMA` takes 6 arguments and returns an `int` handle to an indicator cache rather than a price value. `mt DanielScalper.mq5` passes 7 arguments (the legacy MQL4 signature), causing compilation to fail (`'iMA' - wrong parameters count`). In transpilers or MQL4 emulation where `iMA` returns an integer handle (e.g. 10), assigning it to `double ma` causes `ask > ma` to evaluate whether Ask price is greater than the handle ID integer, completely corrupting market trend logic.
findings.fix: Create the indicator handle in `OnInit()` with `iMA(_Symbol, PERIOD_CURRENT, MAPeriod, 0, MODE_SMA, PRICE_CLOSE)`, allocate a buffer array, and fetch values with `CopyBuffer(handle, 0, 0, 1, buffer)` in `OnTick()`.

findings.title: MQL4 `iMA` invocation signature in `mt DanielScalper.mq5` causes compilation failure and corrupted trend evaluation
findings.failure: In MQL5, `iMA` takes 6 arguments and returns an `int` handle to an indicator cache rather than a price value. `mt DanielScalper.mq5` passes 7 arguments (the legacy MQL4 signature), causing compilation to fail (`'iMA' - wrong parameters count`). In transpilers or MQL4 emulation where `iMA` returns an integer handle (e.g. 10), assigning it to `double ma` causes `ask > ma` to evaluate whether Ask price is greater than the handle ID integer, completely corrupting market trend logic.
findings.fix: Create the indicator handle in `OnInit()` with `iMA(_Symbol, PERIOD_CURRENT, MAPeriod, 0, MODE_SMA, PRICE_CLOSE)`, allocate a buffer array, and fetch values with `CopyBuffer(handle, 0, 0, 1, buffer)` in `OnTick()`.

findings.title: Baseline catalog fingerprint and least-privilege role script SHA-256 drift in closure ledger
findings.failure: A deployment engineer, auditor, or automated verification harness verifying database baseline integrity against `CLOSURE_LEDGER_2026-08-23.md` will expect `3a0ff8ac...` for the catalog semantic fingerprint and `e5c2dd54...` for `least_privilege_roles.sql`. When matching against the real code and database, the actual verified fingerprint is `8772e5e7...` and the role script is `17de4669...`, causing release validation tooling or deployment verification scripts to fail closed or misdiagnose an authentic database as tampered/corrupt.
findings.fix: Update `docs/backend/CLOSURE_LEDGER_2026-08-23.md` lines 29-30 to match the canonical baseline values `17de46699761981c7747be190d8b91f178ade24662ad25bfd2774b13a7bc8c1d` and `8772e5e7b8044ef68e185772d569128e771a11fb4b6f06dca7df1260b3822eba`.

findings.title: Anonymous readiness single-flight timeout mismatch between status doc and probe implementation
findings.failure: `ControlPlaneReadinessProbe` explicitly documents that a cold pass re-attesting 4 separate least-privilege logins across 12,000+ catalog rows takes ~3.8s and therefore configures a 10-second internal timeout. However, `ApiFoundation.MapYo4xHealthEndpoints` maps the readiness probe using `ApiHealthOptions.ProbeTimeout` (default 5s, which matches the claim in `IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md`). If a cold-start probe or database load pushes the readiness query between 5.0s and 10.0s, `BoundedBooleanProbe` cancels execution at 5 seconds and caches `unhealthy` for 1 second, causing Kestrel readiness to report HTTP 503 and triggering premature container restarts during cold start.
findings.fix: Update `IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md` to reflect the 10-second deadline, and ensure `ApiHealthOptions.ProbeTimeout` in `YO4X.ControlPlane.Api` is configured to match the 10-second requirement of `ControlPlaneReadinessProbe`.

findings.title: Finding inventory table in MQ5_COMPATIBILITY_REPORT.md reports finding instance count under 'Files' column instead of distinct file count
findings.failure: When a single strategy file contains multiple occurrences of the same finding code (for example, `Trailing Stop on Profit.mq5` has two missing `#include` directives, and 8 files trigger `TRADE_RESULT_CONTROL_FLOW_REVIEW_REQUIRED` twice from both `TRADE_ORDER_SEND` and `TRADE_CTRADE` features), the finding inventory table aggregates total finding object count rather than distinct file count while labeling the column `Files`. Consumers reading the report receive `141` for `TRADE_RESULT_CONTROL_FLOW_REVIEW_REQUIRED` (actual: 133 distinct files) and `7` for `INCLUDE_SOURCE_MISSING` (actual: 6 distinct files).
findings.fix: Update the finding inventory formatter to aggregate distinct file count per finding code (`group.Select(static f => f.FileRelativePath).Distinct().Count()`) or rename the column header to `Occurrences`.

findings.title: ADR 0001 asserts GatewayHost directly references `YO4X.Trading.Mt5` when code enforces process isolation
findings.failure: An engineer referencing ADR 0001 adds code assuming `GatewayHost` directly references `YO4X.Trading.Mt5`. This causes architecture boundary tests (`ArchitectureBoundaryTests.cs:184-185`: `Assert.DoesNotContain("YO4X.Trading.Mt5", projectReferences)`) to fail and break CI, because `GatewayHost` references `YO4X.Trading.ProcessIsolation`, which spawns `YO4X.Mt5.WorkerHost` as an isolated child process over redirected stdin/stdout pipes.
findings.fix: Update ADR 0001 to document that `GatewayHost` references `YO4X.Trading.ProcessIsolation`, and only the worker process `YO4X.Mt5.WorkerHost` references `YO4X.Trading.Mt5`.

findings.title: Design System tokens and typography diverge from frontend code

findings.title: Committed vendor assembly mt5api.dll lacks Authenticode publisher signature and strong-name signing
findings.failure: An operator or CI system loading `mt5api.dll` has no cryptographic attestation linking the compiled MSIL bytecode to a verified publisher identity (`mtapi.online`). While local repository SHA-256 hash checks prevent unauthorized local file replacement, the platform has no publisher-signed provenance proving the binary was built from clean source without upstream build pipeline compromise.
findings.fix: Require the vendor to supply an Authenticode-signed assembly backed by a valid corporate EV certificate, or establish an internal signing and attestation ceremony prior to checking binary artifacts into source control.

findings.title: Missing commercial license, distribution notice, and terms-of-use grant in vendor directory

Deploying or distributing the platform into cloud, SaaS, or commercial environments exposes the project to legal liability and licensing disputes because no legal right of distribution, execution, or commercial use is evidenced within the repository.
findings.fix: Add a committed license manifest (`LICENSE.md` / `NOTICE.md`) in `mt5-net-api-full-binaries-main/` documenting the commercial contract terms, allowed deployment topologies, and redistribution boundaries from `mtapi.online`.

findings.title: `Get-BacktestDetail.ps1` declares `$StrategyId` for backtest route with mismatched docstring
findings.failure: The script queries `/v1/backtests/{id}` but names the parameter `$StrategyId` and copy-pastes the synopsis from `Get-StrategyInputs.ps1`. An operator reading the synopsis who supplies a strategy identifier will query the backtest endpoint with an invalid ID, resulting in a 404 response.
findings.fix: Rename `$StrategyId` to `$BacktestId` and update the synopsis docstring to reflect backtest detail inspection.

findings.title: `Get-BrokerSymbols.ps1` declares unused `$StrategyId` parameter and misleading docstring

findings.title: `Test-BrokerAccountLink.ps1` fails to assert HTTP status and returns success on API failure

Automated test suites or CI runners invoking `Test-BrokerAccountLink.ps1` exit with status 0 (success), falsely reporting that the account link flow succeeded.
findings.fix: Parse the `HTTP_STATUS` token from the curl output and throw an exception or exit with code 1 if the HTTP status is not `200` or `201`.

findings.title: `Test-PostgresIntegration.ps1` fallback hardcodes local author user profile path

The script immediately fails with `dotnet.exe was not found.`.
findings.fix: Replace the hardcoded path with `Join-Path $workspaceRoot ".tools\dotnet-sdk-10.0.400\dotnet.exe"` or dynamically construct the path using `Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "YO4X\dotnet\dotnet.exe"`.

findings.title: Plaintext bearer token persisted in `debug-import-session.ps1` without `finally` cleanup guarantee
findings.failure: `debug-import-session.ps1` writes the active authorization token `$Token` into `.local\development\dbg.cfg`. Because the invocation of `curl.exe` is not wrapped in a `try ... finally` block, any network failure, user interruption (Ctrl+C), or terminating error prior to line 28 leaves the unencrypted bearer token stored on disk in the workspace directory.
findings.fix: Wrap the curl execution and file deletion in a `try ... finally` block to guarantee `$body` and `$cfg` are removed upon exit.

findings.title: Unscoped `DELETE` in `project-corpus-to-catalog.sql` deletes all tenant performance figures
findings.failure: When `Import-Mql5Corpus.ps1` executes `project-corpus-to-catalog.sql` under the `postgres` superuser role, line 101 runs an unqualified `DELETE FROM catalog.strategy_performance;` with no tenant predicate or strategy filter. In a multi-tenant database or a database containing existing strategies from other sources, this statement deletes all performance metrics across all tenants and all strategies rather than only the strategy performance records associated with the projected corpus source files.
findings.fix: Replace the unqualified delete with a scoped delete matching the imported corpus strategies: `DELETE FROM catalog.strategy_performance WHERE strategy_id IN (SELECT id FROM governance.strategy_source_files);`.

findings.title: Untrusted evaluation CancellationTokenSource disposed on host cancellation while background task is running
findings.failure: In `StrategyEventProcessingCoordinator.ExecuteAsync`, `evaluationCancellation` is passed to `Task.Run(() => strategyHost.EvaluateAsync(..., evaluationCancellation.Token))`. If the untrusted host throws an internal `OperationCanceledException` while `cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested` is false, execution enters `catch (OperationCanceledException)` at line 210 without setting `cancellationDisposalDeferred = true`. The `finally` block at lines 226–229 then immediately invokes `evaluationCancellation.Dispose()`. If background evaluation worker threads are still running, accessing the disposed `evaluationCancellation.Token` throws `ObjectDisposedException`.
findings.fix: Set `cancellationDisposalDeferred = true` in all catch blocks where the background `evaluation` task may still be running, and dispose `evaluationCancellation` only via a terminal continuation on `evaluation`.

findings.title: Unobserved Faulted Gateway Tasks on Timeout or Cancellation in Broker Command Coordinator
findings.failure: `gateway.SendAsync(claim.Command, gatewayCancellation.Token)` creates and returns `Task<GatewaySendResult> send`. If `send.WaitAsync(...)` times out or `cancellationToken` cancels, `WaitAsync` throws a `TimeoutException` or `OperationCanceledException` and jumps to `catch (Exception)` at line 287. Unlike the pre-await check at line 248 which calls `_ = ObserveGatewayCompletionAsync(send);`, the catch block does not attach any observation continuation to `send`. If the background send operation subsequently faults with a transport exception, the exception remains unobserved on the underlying task, raising `TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException`. (A symmetric issue exists in `ReconcileAsync` at line 494).
findings.fix: In `BrokerCommandCoordinator.DispatchAsync` and `ReconcileAsync`, register an exception observation continuation (`task.ContinueWith(static t => _ = t.Exception, ...)` or `ObserveGatewayCompletionAsync`) in a `finally` block or inside the catch block whenever `WaitAsync` does not complete successfully.

findings.title: Gateway CancellationTokenSource disposed while background gateway send remains in flight
findings.failure: In `BrokerCommandCoordinator.DispatchAsync`, `gatewayCancellation` is created with a `using` declaration and passed to `gateway.SendAsync(claim.Command, gatewayCancellation.Token)` (line 240). If `send.WaitAsync` times out at line 256 or `cancellationToken` cancels, `DispatchAsync` catches the exception or returns `GatewayTimeoutUnknown`, exiting the `using var gatewayCancellation` block at line 295. Disposing `gatewayCancellation` while `gateway.SendAsync` is still actively executing in the background causes in-flight socket/process operations attempting to register or unregister cancellation callbacks to throw `ObjectDisposedException`. (A symmetric issue exists in `ReconcileAsync` at line 488).
findings.fix: Defer disposal of `gatewayCancellation` until the underlying `send` task finishes by attaching a terminal continuation (`send.ContinueWith(static (_, state) => ((CancellationTokenSource)state!).Dispose(), gatewayCancellation, ...)`), rather than disposing it at the end of the `using` block.

findings.title: Mutation creation endpoints in FrontendProjectionEndpoints lack idempotency precondition filters
findings.failure: When a client issues `POST /v1/bots` or `POST /v1/backtests` and encounters a network timeout or proxy replay, the client retries the request. Because `MutationPreconditionFilter` is not attached to these routes (unlike mutation routes in `Program.cs`), the server creates multiple distinct records with new version 7 GUIDs in `bots.bots` and `simulation.backtests`, resulting in unwanted duplicate bot configurations and redundant backtest executions.
findings.fix: Apply `.AddEndpointFilter(new MutationPreconditionFilter())` to `POST /bots` and `POST /backtests`, and plumb request metadata through to the underlying application to enforce idempotency key deduplication.

findings.title: Duplicated UserActor claims extraction and assurance parsing across endpoint definitions
findings.failure: The identical `ToUserActor(ClaimsPrincipal)` method is copy-pasted in `FrontendProjectionEndpoints.cs:290-306`, `BrokerAccountDiscoveryEndpoints.cs:36-52`, and `Program.cs:541-557`. Future modifications to claim schemas, default assurance handling, or MFA policy mapping in one location risk leaving other endpoints running divergent authentication and tenant extraction logic.
findings.fix: Extract `ToUserActor` into a centralized helper or extension method on `ClaimsPrincipal` in `YO4X.Identity` or `YO4X.ControlPlane.Api` and reference it consistently across all route definitions.

findings.title: `IPAddress.IsLoopback` check rejects IPv4 loopback connections on dual-stack listener during broker account linking
findings.failure: When Kestrel listens on dual-stack sockets (`[::]`), local clients connecting via IPv4 (`127.0.0.1`) produce an IPv4-mapped IPv6 `RemoteIpAddress` (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`). In .NET, `IPAddress.IsLoopback` returns `false` for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses, causing legitimate local requests to `POST /v1/broker-accounts` to be rejected with HTTP 403 `LOCAL_CREDENTIAL_BOUNDARY_REQUIRES_LOOPBACK`.
findings.fix: Unmap IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses before checking loopback: `IPAddress? ip = context.Connection.RemoteIpAddress; if (ip is null || !IPAddress.IsLoopback(ip.IsIPv4MappedToIPv6 ? ip.MapToIPv4() : ip))`.

findings.title: `ClassifySourceNetwork` misclassifies IPv4-mapped loopback connections as private in request metadata
findings.failure: An IPv4 loopback connection arriving on a dual-stack socket (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`) fails the initial `IPAddress.IsLoopback` check. After being unmapped to IPv4 (`127.0.0.1`), execution falls through without re-checking loopback, hitting `bytes[0] == 127` which classifies the network as `"private"` instead of `"loopback"` in audit and request metadata.
findings.fix: Check `IPAddress.IsLoopback` again immediately after unmapping `address.MapToIPv4()`, or map to IPv4 before the initial `IPAddress.IsLoopback` check.

findings.title: Missing `RuntimeEvidencePostgres` is tolerated during registration but permanently fails the readiness probe
findings.failure: If `ConnectionStrings:RuntimeEvidencePostgres` is omitted or invalid, `TryAddRuntimeControlPostgres` skips registering `RuntimeEvidencePostgresDatabase` but continues to register `PostgresRuntimeControlPlaneApplication`. The host starts without errors, but `ControlPlaneReadinessProbe.IsReadyAsync` requires `RuntimeEvidencePostgresDatabase` in DI, causing `/health/ready` to permanently return 503 Service Unavailable.
findings.fix: Make `RuntimeEvidencePostgresDatabase` registration mandatory in `TryAddRuntimeControlPostgres` (returning `services` early without registering `PostgresRuntimeControlPlaneApplication` if evidence database configuration fails) so the host falls back to `UnavailableRuntimeControlPlaneApplication`.

findings.title: Untracked pre-registered `ITenantContextCapabilityProvider` bypasses endpoint validation in `TenantContextCapabilityRegistration`
findings.failure: If `ITenantContextCapabilityProvider` is registered via factory or type descriptor without a `TenantContextCapabilityEndpointRegistration`, `existingProvider.ImplementationInstance` is `null`. `TryAdd` returns `true` unconditionally on line 39 without verifying that the pre-registered provider's endpoint matches `requiredEndpoint`, allowing database pools targeting different endpoints to share an invalid issuer provider.
findings.fix: Reject or require explicit endpoint verification when a pre-existing provider descriptor is present without an inspectable instance or endpoint registration.

findings.title: Missing exponential backoff on repeated dependency or store operation failures in ControlWorkBackgroundService
findings.failure: When a database outage, network partition, or store failure occurs, `RunCycleOnceAsync` records the failure and returns `RequiredDependencyUnavailable` or `StoreOperationFailed`. However, `ExecuteAsync` discards the outcome (`_ = await ...`) and waits only for the fixed `_options.PollInterval` (which can be configured down to 100ms, defaulting to 1s). During sustained outages, the worker loops at maximum polling frequency, repeatedly executing probes and hammering the database without backoff or jitter.
findings.fix: Inspect the `ControlWorkCycleOutcome` returned by `RunCycleOnceAsync` and apply an exponential backoff delay with jitter when consecutive cycles fail.

findings.title: Unchecked `DispatchMessageId!.Value` in worker proof readers crashes reconciliation loop
findings.failure: In `PersistedOperation`, `DispatchMessageId` is declared as nullable `Guid?`, representing the nullable column `control.user_operations.dispatch_message_id`. When `ProcessClaimedOpenOperationAsync` processes operations claimed via `ClaimOpenAsync` in `unknown` state (or `propagating`/`reconciling` where dispatch failed before a dispatch message was recorded), `operation.DispatchMessageId` is `null`. While `ReadDispatchStateAsync` (line 2456) safely checks `if (operation.DispatchMessageId is null) return null;`, `ReadDeploymentProofAsync` (line 2536) and `ReadBrokerProofAsync` (line 2692) unconditionally dereference `operation.DispatchMessageId!.Value`. This throws an unhandled `InvalidOperationException: Nullable object must have a value.` and crashes worker reconciliation.
findings.fix: Add `if (operation.DispatchMessageId is null) { return null; }` at the beginning of both `ReadDeploymentProofAsync` and `ReadBrokerProofAsync` before preparing command parameters.

findings.title: `UserOperationDispatchGuard.IsSha256` throws `NullReferenceException` instead of returning false
findings.failure: If `FixedBindingEquals` is invoked with a null string (such as unpopulated dispatch or target binding properties evaluated in `IsReconciliationBindingCurrent`), `value.Length` dereferences null and throws `NullReferenceException` instead of evaluating to false and cleanly failing closed.
findings.fix: Change `IsSha256` parameter to `string? value` and use pattern matching `value is { Length: 64 } && value.All(...)` consistent with `PostgresDeploymentProjectionStore.cs:873`.

findings.title: WorkerTenantScanLease lifecycle SemaphoreSlim leaked on every cycle disposal
findings.failure: `WorkerTenantScanLease` instantiates `private readonly SemaphoreSlim lifecycleGate = new(1, 1);` on line 96 for every lease created across all background worker workstreams (`Outbox`, `CredentialGrantExpiry`, `DeploymentProjection`, `UserOperations`). In `DisposeAsync()`, `lifecycleGate` is acquired, `consumerGate` is released, and `lifecycleGate` is released, but `lifecycleGate.Dispose()` is never called. Under continuous background worker polling, thousands of unmanaged wait handles are left undisposed and rely entirely on GC finalization.
findings.fix: In `WorkerTenantScanLease.DisposeAsync()`, dispose `lifecycleGate` after releasing it, or avoid allocating a per-lease `SemaphoreSlim` by using a lightweight non-blocking synchronisation mechanism.

findings.title: Premature CancellationTokenSource disposal while background operation is running in WorkerOperationBoundary
findings.failure: When a bounded worker operation exceeds `operationTimeout` or `cancellationToken` cancels, `ExecuteCoreAsync` invokes `ObserveTerminationAsync`. If `operationTask` fails to stop within `cancellationConfirmationTimeout`, the method attaches `_ = ObserveLateCompletionAsync(operationTask);` and throws `WorkerOperationTerminationUnconfirmedException` at line 89. Exiting `ExecuteCoreAsync` triggers the `using var operationCancellation` disposal. Because `operationTask` continues executing in the background, downstream asynchronous calls (such as database command execution or socket streams) that check or register callbacks on `operationCancellation.Token` throw `ObjectDisposedException`, generating unobserved task exceptions and preventing clean asynchronous shutdown.
findings.fix: Defer disposal of `operationCancellation` until `operationTask` reaches a terminal state by registering disposal inside a continuation attached to `operationTask`, rather than disposing it synchronously when `terminationObserved` is false.

findings.title: Liveness probe unconditionally reports healthy when worker workstreams are terminally stopped
findings.failure: When hosted background workstreams (`OutboxDispatch` and `ControlWork`) fail or encounter a fatal unconfirmed termination condition (`WorkerOperationTerminationUnconfirmedException`), their work loops exit and transition `WorkerReadiness` into `RequiredWorkstreamState.Stopped`. While `/health/startup` and `/health/ready` fail closed, the liveness endpoint `/health/live` invokes `GetLive()`, which unconditionally returns HTTP 200 (`Healthy: true`, `process_live`) as long as the ASP.NET Core web host is reachable. Container orchestrators (e.g. Kubernetes) evaluating liveness probes will never restart or replace the dead worker process, stranding the worker in a permanent zombie state where dispatching and control loops are inactive.
findings.fix: Synchronize on `_sync` in `WorkerReadiness.GetLive()` and check `AnyState(RequiredWorkstreamState.Stopped)`. If any required workstream is stopped, return an unhealthy snapshot (`Healthy = false`, code `"worker_stopped"`) so container liveness probes fail and trigger an orchestrator restart.

findings.title: Non-canonical MQL5 header files (.mqh) are omitted from source signal inspection and misclassified as UnknownQuarantined
findings.failure: When quarantine intake processes non-canonical header files (e.g., `TradeHelper.mqh.bak`, `CustomIndicators.mqh.old`, or `Include/Signals.mqh_`), `sourceCandidateExtension` evaluates to `false` because the path check looks only for `.mq5` substrings and ignores `.mqh`. Consequently, `InspectSourceSignals` returns `("not-inspected", [])` and `Classify` categorizes the file as `UnknownQuarantined` instead of `SourceLikeTextCandidate`, silently dropping MQL preprocessor directive and handler detection for all quarantined header variants.
findings.fix: Update `InspectSourceSignals` (line 855) and `Classify` (line 967) to check `relativePath.Contains(".mq5", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) || relativePath.Contains(".mqh", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)`.

findings.title: Undisposed Process instance on external link navigation in Desktop Shell
findings.failure: In `MainWindow.xaml.cs` (lines 99 and 137), `Process.Start(...)` launches the default browser for external HTTPS navigation. `Process.Start` instantiates a `Process` object that wraps an unmanaged OS process handle (`SafeProcessHandle`). The returned instance is neither wrapped in a `using` statement nor explicitly disposed, leaking the process object and OS handle until finalization.
findings.fix: Wrap the call in `using var process = Process.Start(...)` or discard and dispose the returned `Process` object.

findings.title: Middleware ordering in `UseYo4xApiFoundation` strips security headers and `X-Correlation-Id` on exception responses
findings.failure: When an endpoint throws an unhandled exception or a mapped domain/not-found/conflict exception, execution unwinds to `app.UseExceptionHandler()`. In ASP.NET Core, `ExceptionHandlerMiddleware` invokes `HttpResponse.Clear()`, which resets the response and wipes all headers set prior to the exception (including `X-Correlation-Id` added by `CorrelationIdMiddleware`). Because the security headers middleware is registered *after* `app.UseExceptionHandler()`, it is bypassed on the error path. As a result, problem responses (HTTP 404/409/422/500/503) are returned to clients without `Cache-Control: no-store`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Content-Security-Policy`, and the `X-Correlation-Id` HTTP header.
findings.fix: Register security headers and correlation ID using `HttpResponse.OnStarting` or place the security headers middleware before `app.UseExceptionHandler()` and re-apply the correlation header inside `Yo4xExceptionHandler`.

findings.title: `Yo4xExceptionHandler` classifies client-aborted requests as 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` and logs unhandled exceptions
findings.failure: When a client aborts a connection during request execution, an `OperationCanceledException` is thrown. Because `Yo4xExceptionHandler` does not check `httpContext.RequestAborted.IsCancellationRequested` or handle `OperationCanceledException`, it falls through to the wildcard `_ => StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError`. This logs an unhandled error log on normal client cancellations and attempts to write a 500 problem response to an aborted HTTP connection.
findings.fix: Check `if (exception is OperationCanceledException && httpContext.RequestAborted.IsCancellationRequested) return false;` or return early without logging when the request is aborted.

findings.title: `AddYo4xEmergencyAuthentication` omits `IHostEnvironment`, breaking development authority certificate pinning
findings.failure: `AddYo4xEmergencyAuthentication` does not accept `IHostEnvironment? environment` (unlike `AddYo4xUserAndWorkloadAuthentication`) and invokes `ConfigureJwt` with `environment: null`. In `ConfigureJwt` (lines 166–174), when `DevelopmentAuthorityCertificateSha256` is configured in `appsettings.Development.json` for local emergency testing, `environment?.IsDevelopment() != true` evaluates to `true`, causing host startup to unconditionally throw `InvalidOperationException: A development authority certificate pin is valid only for an HTTPS loopback authority in Development.`.
findings.fix: Add `IHostEnvironment? environment = null` to `AddYo4xEmergencyAuthentication` and forward it into `ConfigureJwt(options, configuration, "Emergency", environment)`.

findings.title: `ClientCertificateFilter` compares local `DateTime` certificate expiration timestamps against `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`
findings.failure: In .NET, `X509Certificate2.NotBefore` and `NotAfter` return `DateTime` in the local system time zone (or with `DateTimeKind.Unspecified`). Direct relational comparisons against `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` implicitly convert `DateTime` to `DateTimeOffset` using the host machine's local time zone offset. On hosts running with non-UTC local time offsets, newly generated valid certificates are falsely rejected as not yet active, or expired certificates remain accepted until the local offset margin passes.
findings.fix: Use `certificate.GetNotBefore()` and `certificate.GetNotAfter()` (or `certificate.NotBefore.ToUniversalTime()` and `certificate.NotAfter.ToUniversalTime()`).

findings.title: `CorrelationIdMiddleware.Get` generates unpersisted ephemeral IDs when invoked on uninitialized contexts
findings.failure: If `CorrelationIdMiddleware.Get(context)` is called on an `HttpContext` before `CorrelationIdMiddleware` has run (or outside the standard pipeline), it creates a new ID but does not write it back to `context.Items[ItemKey]`. Subsequent calls within the same request lifecycle (e.g. logging vs. problem details serialization) each generate different GUIDs, causing logged correlation IDs to mismatch response payload correlation IDs.
findings.fix: Store the newly created correlation ID in `context.Items[ItemKey]` before returning it: `string generated = CreateCorrelationId(); context.Items[ItemKey] = generated; return generated;`.

findings.title: Expired Single-Flight Probe Returns Stale Result and Prevents Future Probes on Hung Dependency
findings.failure: When `probeTask` exceeds `probeTimeout`, `PublishSnapshot` is called with `releaseSingleFlight: false`, which publishes a `false` snapshot with timestamp $T_0$ and completes `completion.Task`, but deliberately leaves `inFlight = completion.Task`. If the underlying probe delegate hangs (e.g. hung network socket), `ExecuteProbeAsync` awaits `ObserveLateProbeAsync` until that underlying task finishes. After the cache `lifetime` expires at $T_0 + \text{lifetime}$, subsequent callers calling `GetAsync` see that `lastCompleted` has expired, but `inFlight` is still referencing the completed `completion.Task`. As a result, `GetAsync` returns `inFlight` directly without initiating a new probe, immediately returning stale `false` snapshots indefinitely until the late task unblocks.
findings.fix: In `PublishSnapshot`, clear `inFlight = null` whenever `completion.TrySetResult` is invoked so subsequent callers past the cache lifetime can schedule a new probe even if a previous late probe is still running.

findings.title: Redundant Thread-Pool Dispatch of Already-Asynchronous Delegate in Bounded Boolean Probe
findings.failure: `BoundedBooleanProbe` accepts `Func<CancellationToken, ValueTask<bool>> probe`. In `ExecuteProbeAsync`, it passes an async lambda that awaits `probe(...)` into `Task.Run`. This allocates an extra closure, schedules an unnecessary thread-pool work item, and creates an extra wrapper `Task` around an operation that is already asynchronous (`ValueTask<bool>`). On high-frequency health probes, this causes unnecessary thread hops and allocation overhead.
findings.fix: Invoke `probe(timeout.Token).AsTask()` directly instead of wrapping the call inside `Task.Run(async () => ...)`.

findings.title: OperationResult.Failure with empty params evaluates to IsSuccess == true
findings.failure: Invoking `OperationResult.Failure<T>()` without arguments or passing an empty array `OperationResult.Failure<T>([])` creates an `OperationResult<T>` with `Errors.Count == 0`. `IsSuccess` evaluates `Errors.Count == 0` to `true`, causing callers checking `if (result.IsSuccess)` to treat an explicitly failed operation as successful with an uninitialized `default(T)` value.
findings.fix: Enforce at least one error either by validating `if (errors.Length == 0) throw new ArgumentException(...)` or by changing the signature to `Failure<T>(OperationError error, params OperationError[] additionalErrors)`.

findings.title: OperationResult<T> exposes unguarded Value getter on failure results
findings.failure: `OperationResult<T>` is a positional record exposing `Value` directly. When an operation fails, `Value` returns `default(T)` without throwing. For value types such as `int`, `bool`, or `double`, callers that omit the `IsSuccess` check can silently read `0` or `false` as valid business values rather than failing fast.
findings.fix: Implement an explicit getter for `Value` that throws `InvalidOperationException("Cannot access Value on a failed OperationResult.")` when `!IsSuccess`.

findings.title: FixedClock.UtcNow property setter does not normalize non-UTC offsets to UTC
findings.failure: While the constructor calls `.ToUniversalTime()`, mutating `fixedClock.UtcNow = new DateTimeOffset(2026, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0, TimeSpan.FromHours(5))` assigns the value directly to the auto-property without normalization. Subsequent reads from `IClock.UtcNow` return a timestamp with `Offset == +05:00` instead of `TimeSpan.Zero`, violating the UTC contract expected by domain and time-series consumers.
findings.fix: Back `UtcNow` with a private field and call `value.ToUniversalTime()` in the property setter.

findings.title: Trade journal database schema `numeric(18,5)` truncates sub-pip and crypto prices
findings.failure: For crypto symbols priced below $1 (e.g. DOGE, SHIB, ADA at `$0.00001234`) or 6-digit fractional pip forex feeds, storing trade records in PostgreSQL truncates prices beyond 5 decimal places to `0.00001`, corrupting recorded execution history and P&L attribution.
findings.fix: Migrate `entry_price` and `exit_price` in `journal.trades` to `numeric(18,8)`.

findings.title: Missing queue lease timeout mechanism in backtest queue causes permanent worker stall on crash
findings.failure: When a background worker claims a backtest with `status = 'QUEUED'` via `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and transitions it to `status = 'RUNNING'`, the row leaves the partial index `backtests_queued_claim_idx`. Migration 008 introduces no worker claim lease timestamp (such as `lease_expires_at` or `heartbeat_at`), visibility timeout, or retry attempt counter. If the worker process crashes, encounters an OOM/fatal termination, or hangs during execution, the row remains in `status = 'RUNNING'` indefinitely. Because the claim index and runner claim query only evaluate `WHERE status = 'QUEUED'`, no subsequent worker can ever detect, reclaim, or fail the abandoned run, permanently stranding the backtest in the user's dashboard.
findings.fix: Add a `lease_expires_at timestamptz` column to `simulation.backtests` and adjust the claim/reclaim query and partial index to include timed-out running jobs (`WHERE status = 'QUEUED' OR (status = 'RUNNING' AND lease_expires_at < clock_timestamp())`).

findings.title: Missing positive check constraint on `simulation.backtests.equity_initial_deposit` permits zero and negative initial capital
findings.failure: `equity_initial_deposit` lacks a `check (equity_initial_deposit > 0)` constraint, unlike `contract_size`, `volume`, and `equity_decimation_interval` which have explicit positive checks. An invalid payload or corrupted worker result can persist `equity_initial_deposit = 0.0000` or negative values alongside valid sample counts. When the frontend or reporting calculation computes percentage returns or drawdown baselines against `equity_initial_deposit`, division by zero or negative baseline calculations result in `NaN` / `Infinity` or reversed return metrics.
findings.fix: Add `check (equity_initial_deposit > 0)` to `simulation.backtests.equity_initial_deposit`.

findings.title: 3-character ISO constraint on `bots.broker_symbols.currency` rejects standard 4-character crypto and stablecoin quote currencies
findings.failure: On MetaTrader 5 broker servers offering cryptocurrency contracts, instruments are frequently denominated, margined, or settled in 4-character stablecoins or tokens (such as `USDT`, `USDC`, or `FDUSD`). When the broker symbol importer attempts to insert a symbol with `currency = 'USDT'`, the `char(3)` length limit and regex `check (currency ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$')` reject the value, causing symbol catalog synchronization to fail with a `check_violation` or string length error for all Tether and USD Coin denominated trading pairs.
findings.fix: Update `currency` in `bots.broker_symbols` to `text check (currency ~ '^[A-Z0-9]{3,10}$')` or `varchar(10)` to support standard multi-character crypto and stablecoin currency codes.

findings.title: `volume_step` and `volume_min` `numeric(12,2)` precision causes arithmetic underflow and constraint violation for crypto and micro-lot instruments
findings.failure: MetaTrader 5 brokers offering cryptocurrency pairs (such as `BTCUSD` or `ETHUSD`) or micro-lot fractional instruments specify lot steps (`SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP`) and minimum volumes (`SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN`) with 3 to 5 decimal places (e.g. `0.001` or `0.0001` lots). In `bots.broker_symbols`, these columns are constrained to `numeric(12,2)`. When importing broker symbols with a volume step of `0.001`, rounding to 2 decimal places produces `0.00`, which immediately violates `CHECK (volume_step > 0)` and `CHECK (volume_min > 0)`, throwing a PostgreSQL `check_violation` (23514) error and aborting the entire broker instrument import transaction.
findings.fix: Change `volume_min`, `volume_max`, and `volume_step` column types in `bots.broker_symbols` (and `volume` in `bots.bots`) to `numeric(18,4)` or `numeric(18,8)` to accommodate fractional volume steps.

findings.title: Missing upper bound safety constraint on `bots.bots.volume` allows storing unbounded lot sizes driving live orders
findings.failure: `bots.bots.volume` represents the trade volume executed by live trading bots. While line 38 checks `volume > 0`, it enforces no upper bound (e.g. `check (volume between 0.01 and 1000.00)`). If an operator submits a typo (e.g. `50000.00` instead of `0.50`) or a corrupted API request payload is processed, the database stores the massive lot size. When the bot executes live market orders, it submits extreme position sizes directly to the broker gateway, risking account margin blowout and immediate liquidation.
findings.fix: Add a sane upper bound check constraint to `bots.bots.volume`, such as `check (volume > 0 and volume <= 10000.00)`.

findings.title: Redundant B-Tree index on `bots.bot_inputs (tenant_id, bot_id, name)` creates duplicate index maintenance overhead
findings.failure: Line 72 defines table constraint `unique (tenant_id, bot_id, name)`, which automatically builds a backing unique B-tree index on `(tenant_id, bot_id, name)`. Lines 77-78 then explicitly execute `create index bot_inputs_tenant_bot_idx on bots.bot_inputs (tenant_id, bot_id, name)`. This creates a completely redundant second index on the exact same column tuple, adding double write and maintenance overhead on every `bot_inputs` insert, update, and delete without providing any query planner benefit.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate `create index bot_inputs_tenant_bot_idx` statement from `010_bot_settings_and_broker_symbols.sql`.

findings.title: Hardcoded 8-schema scope in privilege extraction causes false accept of broad grants in external schemas
findings.failure: In `PostgresRoleCapabilityFingerprint.Sql`, the CTEs `actual_schema`, `actual_table`, `actual_column_rows`, and `actual_function` strictly filter `where namespace.nspname in ('identity', 'authorization', 'control', 'operations', 'governance', 'audit', 'messaging', 'readmodel')`. When migrations 005–010 introduced external schemas (`catalog`, `bots`, `simulation`, `journal`, `billing`, `brokerdirectory`), `least_privilege_roles.sql:1892-1903` granted `USAGE` and table-wide `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` across all these schemas to `yo4x_control_api` and `yo4x_worker`. However, `Yo4xPostgresRoleContracts.ControlApi` and `Yo4xPostgresRoleContracts.Worker` omit these schemas from `TablePrivileges` and `SchemaPrivileges`. Because `actual_table` ignores all relations outside the 8 core schemas, `(select value from actual_table) = @table_privileges` evaluates to `true`. If an attacker or misconfigured migration grants full table CRUD or schema usage on `billing.cloud_plans`, `bots.bots`, or `simulation.backtests` to restricted roles (e.g. `yo4x_gateway_runtime` or `yo4x_supervisor_runtime`), `PostgresRoleCapabilityFingerprint.IsSatisfiedAsync` falsely accepts the role and passes readiness checks.
findings.fix: Remove the hardcoded 8-schema `where namespace.nspname in (...)` restriction from `actual_schema`, `actual_table`, `actual_column_rows`, and `actual_function` (filtering out only internal PostgreSQL system namespaces like `information_schema` and `^pg_`), and update all role capability contracts in `Yo4xPostgresRoleContracts` to explicitly enumerate their external schema and relation privileges.

findings.title: Role configuration array comparison omits C collation, causing false rejection under localized database collations
findings.failure: In `role_identity`, `order by setting` sorts role GUC configuration settings using the database cluster's default collation (e.g. `en_US.UTF-8`), where punctuation characters like `_` and `=` have different sorting precedence than ASCII byte order. Conversely, `PostgresRoleCapabilityContract.Normalize` sorts GUC strings in C# using `StringComparer.Ordinal` (ASCII). On databases initialized with non-C collations, the ordering of configuration arrays (such as `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=10s`, `lock_timeout=2s`, `statement_timeout=5s`) diverges between PostgreSQL and .NET. When `(select configuration from role_identity) = @role_configuration` executes at line 1834, array equality fails due to mismatched element ordering, falsely rejecting valid database roles and causing application startup failure.
findings.fix: Append `collate "C"` to the sorting expression in line 1644: `select array_agg(setting order by setting collate "C")`.

findings.title: Synchronous full-catalog SHA-256 computation inside every tenant transaction causes severe hot-path latency
findings.failure: In `UserOperationProtocolPostgresDatabases.BeginTenantTransactionAsync` and `RuntimeEvidencePostgresDatabase.BeginTenantTransactionAsync`, every transactional operation invokes `PostgresRoleCapabilityFingerprint.IsSatisfiedAsync(transaction, contract)`. This executes `PostgresCatalogSemanticFingerprint.Sql` (1,026 lines of catalog CTEs iterating over every table, column, policy, trigger definition, and ACL across the database) and streams thousands of rows to C# to incrementally compute a SHA-256 hash. Under high user operation or worker event throughput, this incurs massive database CPU load, heavy catalog lock contention, 50–500ms transaction start overhead, and frequent `statement_timeout` aborts on high-frequency trading and operation dispatch paths.
findings.fix: Perform the full-catalog semantic fingerprint attestation during application startup and periodic background health checks, or cache the catalog attestation result per connection session instead of re-executing whole-catalog hashing inside per-operation transactions.

findings.title: Unregistered database roles and grantees in external schemas bypass catalog semantic fingerprint
findings.failure: In `PostgresCatalogSemanticFingerprint.Sql`, catalog ACL queries for non-core schemas (`external-schema-runtime-acl`, `external-relation-runtime-acl`, `external-function-runtime-acl`) join against `named_yo4x_role`, which hardcodes exactly 16 role names. Furthermore, role existence entries are only collected for roles in `named_yo4x_role`. If a rogue or unmanaged role (e.g. `yo4x_temp`, `backtest_runner`, or an attacker-created user) is created and granted `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on `catalog.strategies`, `bots.bots`, or `simulation.backtests`, the catalog fingerprint query completely ignores the role and its grants. The computed SHA-256 continues to match `ExpectedSha256`, masking unauthorized database privileges in external schemas.
findings.fix: In `PostgresCatalogSemanticFingerprint.Sql`, collect entries for all non-system database roles in `pg_roles` and extract runtime ACLs for all non-internal grantees across external schemas rather than filtering by the static 16-role list.

findings.title: Role capability contracts omit type, domain, language, and tablespace capability checks
findings.failure: `PostgresRoleCapabilityFingerprint.Sql` verifies privileges only across databases, schemas, tables, columns, and functions. It does not extract or assert role grants for `pg_type` (`USAGE ON TYPE/DOMAIN`), `pg_language` (`USAGE ON LANGUAGE`, e.g. `plpgsql`, `c`, `plpython3u`), `pg_tablespace`, or `pg_parameter_acl`. If a runtime role is granted `USAGE ON LANGUAGE` or permissions on custom types/domains, `PostgresRoleCapabilityFingerprint` cannot detect or reject the privilege drift, allowing roles to accumulate untracked non-relation capabilities.
findings.fix: Extend `PostgresRoleCapabilityContract` and `PostgresRoleCapabilityFingerprint.Sql` to include `actual_type` and `actual_language` checks against declarative contract manifests.

findings.title: Absence of defensive statement, lock, and idle timeouts in ControlApi, Worker, and AdminBff contracts
findings.failure: `BaseRoleConfiguration` sets only `transaction_timeout=2min`. While runtime service contracts (`SupervisorRuntime`, `GatewayRuntime`, `CredentialRuntime`, `LocalIdentity`, `ContextIssuer`) explicitly configure `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=10s`, `lock_timeout=2s`, and `statement_timeout=5s`, the three broadest roles (`ControlApi`, `AdminBff`, and `Worker`) omit these three settings. A hung client connection, unindexed slow query, or lock acquisition contention on `yo4x_control_api` or `yo4x_worker` can hold database locks for up to 2 minutes, blocking transaction throughput across the engine.
findings.fix: Add `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout`, `lock_timeout`, and `statement_timeout` to `BaseRoleConfiguration` or explicitly attach them to `ControlApi`, `AdminBff`, and `Worker` contracts.

findings.title: Missing row-level security on 16 tenant projection tables permits cross-tenant data access under `yo4x_control_api`
findings.failure: Across migrations 005, 006, 009, and 010, 16 tenant-scoped tables (`catalog.strategies`, `catalog.strategy_performance`, `catalog.strategy_equity_points`, `catalog.strategy_reviews`, `catalog.strategy_inputs`, `catalog.strategy_enum_members`, `bots.bots`, `bots.bot_metrics`, `bots.uptime_samples`, `bots.bot_inputs`, `bots.broker_symbols`, `simulation.backtests`, `simulation.backtest_inputs`, `simulation.backtest_equity_points`, `billing.cloud_runners`, `journal.trades`) are created without `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, or tenant isolation policies. `least_privilege_roles.sql` then grants unconstrained `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` across all these schemas to `yo4x_control_api` (and `yo4x_worker` receives table-wide write access on `simulation.backtest_equity_points`). Any control-plane endpoint query or background runner task that fails to explicitly predicate `WHERE tenant_id = @tenant_id` reads, modifies, or deletes records belonging to other tenants without database-level enforcement, directly violating the platform tenant boundary.
findings.fix: Add `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, and restrictive tenant policies (`tenant_id = (select control.current_tenant_id())`) to all 16 projection tables in `least_privilege_roles.sql` or their respective migrations.

findings.title: Unrestricted table-level CRUD on global billing configuration tables granted to web API role
findings.failure: In `005_frontend_projections.sql:240-279`, `billing.cloud_regions`, `billing.cloud_plans`, and `billing.cloud_plan_features` define catalogue-wide cloud regions and global plan pricing tiers (where `tenant_id` is null or nonexistent). Granting blanket `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA billing` allows the runtime web API login (`yo4x_control_api`) to execute arbitrary `UPDATE` or `DELETE` statements against global pricing plans and cloud region catalogs, risking platform-wide billing data tampering from a compromised user-facing API instance.
findings.fix: Revoke table-wide write grants on `billing.cloud_regions`, `billing.cloud_plans`, and `billing.cloud_plan_features` from `yo4x_control_api`, granting `SELECT` only on catalogue definitions and restricting `INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` exclusively to `billing.cloud_runners`.

findings.title: Ownership normalization hardcodes core 8 schemas, leaving projection and directory objects owned by bootstrap superuser
findings.failure: The ownership normalization loop in lines 1049–1160 only iterates over the initial 8 schemas. The schemas and relations added in migrations 005 and 007 (`catalog`, `bots`, `simulation`, `journal`, `billing`, `brokerdirectory`) are never transferred to `yo4x_migrator` and remain owned by the offline superuser (`postgres`). This breaks the architectural guarantee that all application schemas and relations are owned by the non-login `yo4x_migrator` role, leaving object-level DDL ownership attached to the superuser identity.
findings.fix: Expand the schema filter array in lines 1053 and 1069 to include `'catalog', 'bots', 'simulation', 'journal', 'billing', 'brokerdirectory'` so all application objects are normalized to `yo4x_migrator`.

findings.title: `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` lacks coverage for objects created by migration superuser in external schemas
findings.failure: `least_privilege_roles.sql` only configures `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE yo4x_migrator` and `yo4x_context_authority`. Because migrations run under an offline superuser session (e.g. `postgres`), future objects created during migrations do not inherit default privilege revocations from the migrator role. Furthermore, no default privilege rules grant access to `yo4x_control_api` or `yo4x_worker` in projection schemas, forcing every newly added table to either duplicate explicit grants in `least_privilege_roles.sql` or fail closed with 42501 permission denied upon deployment.
findings.fix: Execute `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES REVOKE ALL ON TABLES/SEQUENCES/FUNCTIONS FROM PUBLIC` without role qualification during the superuser deployment session, or enforce `SET ROLE yo4x_migrator` within DDL migrations.

findings.title: Absence of granular transaction, lock, and statement timeouts for `yo4x_control_api` and `yo4x_worker`
